 Order

The petitioner-accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in Crime No.355/2024 of Hebbagodi Police Station, pending on the file of the learned II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323,
376, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Abhilasha.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri. Lethif B., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent -State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:27274 REASONS 4.
Petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 30.05.2024 and since then he is in judicial custody.
The victim aged 29 years has filed the complaint.
It is her contention that during 2012, she came to Bengaluru and started to reside with the family of the petitioner.
Petitioner is said to have committed rape on her during 2013 and subsequently on various occasions.
She married one Sunil Kumar on 27.01.2019.
It is stated that the petitioner is the maternal uncle of the said Sunil Kumar.
The victim alleges that on 24.05.2024, again the petitioner attempted to commit rape on her and she filed complaint on 29.05.2024.
In the meantime, on 01.06.2024, the husband of the informant-Sunil Kumar said to have lodged complaint against her.
It is stated that FIR was not registered on the basis of the said complaint and only NCR was issued.
After apprehending the petitioner, he was subjected to interrogation.

Even though investigation is still in progress, it is not the contention of the prosecution that the petitioner is to be detained in custody for any purpose except to ensure his presence before the trial Court.
Hence, I am of the opinion that NC: 2024:KHC:27274 the petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.
5. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.355/2024 of Hebbagodi Police Station, on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court,
Venkatesh H S vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145620785/
2 subject to the following conditions:
a). The petitioner shall not commit similar offences.
b). The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when required.
NC: 2024:KHC:27274 If in case, the petitioner violates any of the conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to move the Trial Court seeking cancellation of bail.

On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Trial Court is at liberty to direct the Investigating Officer to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by the petitioner and the sureties and a report may be called for in that regard, which is to be submitted by the Investigating Officer within 5 days.
The Trial Court on satisfaction, may proceed to accept the sureties for the purpose of releasing the petitioner on bail.
